headline: High-risk pair: nullclaw can write and exfiltrate workspace data while caveman ingests MCP/file content, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw exposes MCP, file, stdin/stdout, browser, and webhook surfaces, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content; caveman also uses MCP and reads project files like CLAUDE.md and memory files. The pair has a plausible instruction-hijack path through shared content, though no direct shared channel is documented, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF nullclaw forwards untrusted webhook, browser, or file content into MCP prompts
IF caveman reads CLAUDE.md or memory files produced by nullclaw without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces
Disable MCP on one side during cross-agent tasks
Add a provenance prefix to all inter-agent files
Review any shared prompt or note before reuse
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and workspace files, while caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md. nullclaw has broad network egress and file access, so sensitive data can flow out of the shared workspace into external services by default; caveman can then read or propagate those artifacts.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF nullclaw is given any secret-bearing file or webhook payload
IF caveman reads files written by nullclaw without redaction
mitigations: Move secrets out of the shared workspace
Rotate any exposed tokens before pairing
Restrict nullclaw to a redacted subdirectory
Audit files written by either agent after each run
requires-engineering: add per-file secret scanning before handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both can write or modify shared state: nullclaw can write the filesystem and modify git state, while caveman can use MCP and multiple instances. With overlapping mutable surfaces and no locking described, concurrent edits to the same repo or workspace can clobber each other in default use.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git repository
IF nullclaw and caveman run concurrently
IF either agent writes files that the other also edits
mitigations: Run only one agent at a time on shared files
Use separate git branches per agent
Lock the workspace during writes
Check git diff before merging outputs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level file locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can produce webhook, agent-card, and workspace outputs that caveman can ingest through files or MCP, and caveman is a content-writing agent likely to reuse those outputs. Because the pair lacks a documented verification step, false or malicious content from nullclaw can cascade into caveman-generated artifacts or actions.
conditions: IF caveman treats nullclaw-generated notes or files as authoritative
IF nullclaw emits malformed or adversarial content into shared files
IF downstream output is published without human review
mitigations: Require human review before publishing downstream output
Mark inter-agent files as untrusted
Add a verification checklist for imported facts
Compare outputs against source material before reuse
requires-engineering: add signed provenance for agent outputs

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and audit logs, while caveman touches session logs, memory files, and project notes. The pair therefore creates a plausible retention and secret-handling mismatch in shared workspaces, even though no specific residency regime is documented for either agent.
conditions: IF regulated or secret-bearing data is stored in the shared workspace
IF either agent retains logs longer than the other
IF deletion or export requests must cover both agents' artifacts
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Set a short manual log-retention window
Delete temporary files after each task
Document which agent owns each data class
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
